passages.note: Senate concurrence/final passage vote, Grover Yea; 6 of 29 voted No, so not near-unanimous.

passages.provision_quote: without written parental consent make changes to a student's education record
passages.note: Operative text guarantees parental access to the education record and requires parental consent to change the record's gender identity; it neither requires proactive notification (rung 4) nor governs staff use of names or pronouns (rung 5's object), so it shows only the parental-involvement side.

rows.reasoning: Grover voted Yea on S.B. 100 (2023), which bars schools from shielding a student's education record from parents and forbids changing the record's gender identity "without written parental consent". That puts him on the parental side, but the bill's object is the education record: it does not "Require schools to notify parents" nor "Require parental permission before staff use a different name or pronouns", and its consent clause goes beyond merely telling parents "when parents ask", so no single rung is matched clause for clause.
